title: Two concurrent transitions on one case admit exactly one winner
risk: Two operators act on the same case simultaneously, so the case ends in an impossible state and one operator's work silently disappears.
preconditions: An IN_PROGRESS case CASE-T1-0010 for cust-a in namespace cd-race-*
Two concurrent transition requests issued at 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z by CS-01 (to RESOLVED) and op-7 (to WAITING_CUSTOMER)

steps.action: Issue both transitions concurrently against the same case version
steps.expected: exactly one request succeeds and the other is rejected as a stale/concurrent transition

steps.action: Read the resulting case state and its version
steps.expected: the case holds exactly one of the two target states and the version advanced by exactly one

steps.action: Replay the losing request after the winner committed
steps.expected: the replay is refused against the new version and still does not change the state

steps.action: Read the audit trail for the case
steps.expected: one accepted transition entry and at least one refused entry exist, each naming its actor

assertions: Exactly one of the two concurrent transitions is accepted; the case version increases by exactly 1
The losing request is refused without any partial write (no orphan resolution or reason field)
The audit trail records both the accepted and the refused attempt with actor identity
forbidden: Apply both transitions so the case ends with a resolution and a waiting reason at once
Let the losing request overwrite the winner's fields without a version check
evidence: Case state, version and field-level projection after the race
Audit entries for both attempts with accepted/refused status

automation: Issue the two requests from two worker threads against the real case service behind the tenant-scoped wrapper; the version column and the field projection are the oracle, so a last-writer-wins implementation fails.
